title: OSD device descriptor 0.6
description: How a synthesizer, drum machine, controller or music software speaks MIDI or OSC: its identity, controls, messages, programs and drum sounds, with where each piece of data comes from. One file per device and source; a firmware with its own MIDI is its own file. Fields starting with _ are notes for people.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

capabilities.description: What a reader needs beyond the declarative fields. A closed list, today lua (a Lua expression or script). The reader derives the list from the fields present and refuses a declared list that differs; decode lua requires lua.

role_vocabulary.description: The state of the vocabulary of roles (schemas/vocabulary/<state>/) every role of the descriptor is written with; required when a control carries a role. The reader refuses a state it does not hold.

midi_of.description: The descriptor whose MIDI this firmware answers to unchanged (its id, maker/file without .json): this file then only says what differs.

loads_sounds_of.description: Devices (their address prefix without /) whose sounds this one loads as they are.

sound_transfers.description: What in a message is the sound: for each form a sound travels in (alone, in a bank), the elements of the message. The identity of a sound is the SHA-256 of its data element alone.

selects.description: What a program change selects: the sound kind's list, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as a plain recall).

requires.description: Settings on the device needed first, as its manual names them.

after.description: Messages sent after a recall (before it for before); with program_change false, before and after recall alone.

recall_script.description: A Lua script that writes the recall itself, in place of before, the bank select, the program change and after: it reads ctx (channel, dev, family, member, bank, bank_name, msb, lsb, program, index, number) and returns the messages, a list of lists of bytes. Requires the lua capability.

script.description: A Lua script that writes the request that reads a sound back: it reads ctx like recall_script and returns one list of bytes. Requires the lua capability.

reply_timeout_ms.description: How long the device may take to answer the request, in milliseconds; never shorter than programs.delay_ms (the reader refuses it).

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

dump.description: How the current sound is taken from it.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

programs.description: Its programs and banks: how to select one, how they are numbered, how a sound is taken from it.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sysex.description: The bytes every SysEx message of the device starts and ends with.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

cc_params.description: Controls set by Control Change, 14-bit CC pairs, NRPN or RPN.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

params.description: Parameters read and written by SysEx through one shared message shape. get_frame, set_frame and value_type are required, except in a file with midi_of, which takes them from its target.

commands.description: Named messages: SysEx utilities, or OSC messages of a software.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

triggers.description: Drum and sample sounds fired by a note.

note_offset.description: Added to every note number sent.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

midi_out.description: Playing it: notes, pitch bend, aftertouch, program change.

midi_in.description: osc-bridge extension: the MIDI messages the device sends while played and that are reported, each at the OSC address the specification fixes, under the device's prefix; what follows the space are the OSC arguments, in this order. note_on: /note/on {note} {velocity} {channel}. note_off: /note/off {note} {velocity} {channel}. cc: /cc/{num} {value} {channel}. pitchbend: /pitchbend {value_u14} {channel}. aftertouch: /aftertouch {value} {channel}. poly_aftertouch: /poly_aftertouch {note} {value} {channel}. program_change: /program_change {program} {channel}. An empty list reports nothing.

replies.description: Messages the device answers or sends by itself, recognised.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

subscriptions.description: OSC messages a software needs at start to report its changes.

osc.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix.

script.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua script that builds the message.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

custom_commands.description: osc-bridge extension: addresses handled by a script only.

_sources.description: Where the data comes from, with its credit, licence and the firmware it documents.

id.description: The name of this form of transfer, the one a reader is asked for.

sound_id.description: Declares that the data of this form is the same as that of every form of the device with the same sound_id: a sound alone and the same sound in a bank.

carries.description: One sound, or a bank of sounds.

match_frame.description: The message recognised, one element per byte: the message is as long as this list.

count.description: A bank: the number of sounds it carries.

stride.description: A bank: the sound i has its elements shifted by i times stride bytes.

settings.description: Where the value of each control lies in the data of a sound of this form: a list of settings, each pointing to the control it sets. A control carries no place.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

control.description: The JSON pointer of the control this setting sets: an entry of cc_params or of params.

from.description: The first byte of the place in the data of the sound (unpacked, the name left out; the first byte is 0).

length.description: The number of bytes of the place. The value of a whole-byte place is the unsigned integer of the bytes, the first the highest; the reader reads up to 8 bytes.

bits_per_byte.description: The value is made of the 7 low bits of each byte of the place (a 14-bit value on two bytes of 7 bits).

script.description: A Lua script that gives the value from the data. Requires the lua capability.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sound_setting.description: A control and its place in the data of the sound: whole bytes ({from, length}), bits of them (bits), 7-bit words (bits_per_byte), or a Lua script ({script}); a place and a script never together.

from.description: The first bit; 0 is the lowest bit of the first byte of the place.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sound_setting_bits.description: Bits of the bytes of a place.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sound_elements.description: The data (what makes the sound), the name, and the transport parts (channel, device number, header, checksum, bank and program number); only the data enters the identity.

from.description: The first byte of the element in the message (F0 is 0).

script.description: A Lua script that gives the element from the message. Requires the lua capability.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sound_element.description: An element found by positions ({from, length}) or by a Lua script ({script}), never both.

from.description: The first byte of the data in the message (F0 is 0).

length.description: The number of bytes in the message.

packing.description: How the data is packed in 7 bits: none (default), or msb_first_7in8, a byte of the high bits then 7 bytes of 7 bits, as the KORG minilogue xd MIDI implementation (note 1, 7 bit data format conversion) writes it; the last group may be partial. Any other packing is given by a script.

script.description: A Lua script that gives the data from the message. Requires the lua capability.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

sound_data_element.description: The data of the sound, found by positions ({from, length}, with its packing) or by a Lua script ({script}), never both.

parts.description: The path of the role: the parts from the outermost to the innermost, each with its number when the instrument has several. The text of this path, in the CamelCase segments of a Property Exchange paramPath (M2-117-UM), is what osd gives and reads back.

setting.description: What is set on the part: a term of type setting of the vocabulary state the descriptor names, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term>.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

role.description: What a control does, in the words every device shares: a path of parts ending in a setting. The reader checks each term against the state named by role_vocabulary, that each part stands under the one before it (stands_under, at_top) and that the setting applies to the last part.

part.description: A part of the instrument: a term of type part of the vocabulary state the descriptor names, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term>.

index.description: The number of the part, from 1, when the instrument has several.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

role_part.description: A part in the path of a role, with its number when the instrument has several.

capture_segment.description: A capture in an address: the part of the address that takes the value of the field of this name.

segments.description: An address with captures: the concatenation of its segments, never split on a slash. At least one capture, at most 16 segments; an address without capture is a string.

allOf.$comment: two captures side by side are ambiguous where an address is recognised: none of the 15 pairs of neighbours (the bound is 16 segments) is two objects

emitted_address.description: An address emitted: a string without brace, or an array of segments (a string without brace or a capture); captures may sit side by side.

recognised_address.description: An address recognised: a string without brace, or an array of segments with no two captures side by side.

command_address.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix: a string starting with / and without brace, or segments whose first is a string starting with /.

oneOf.description: The value of an argument of the command.

osc_value.description: An OSC argument: a JSON literal, {"arg": name} (an argument of the command) or {"capture": name} (a field captured in the message).

frame_part.description: An element of a frame that is not a byte: an object of one key of its nature, with the keys that qualify it.

oneOf.title: arg
oneOf.description: An argument of the command, with its encoding, or an offset added to a 7-bit argument (the sum wraps on 7 bits).

oneOf.title: device_id
oneOf.description: The device id, by the rule of identity.device_id with its default value.

oneOf.title: identity
oneOf.description: The bytes of the model's family or member: all of them, or the one at index.

oneOf.title: checksum
oneOf.description: The checksum of the bytes written from offset from (F0 is 0), on length bytes when given: twos7 is Roland's two's complement, sum7 Waldorf's sum, xor7 Fractal's xor, each on 7 bits.

frame_token.description: An element of a message sent: a byte, or an object of one key of its nature (arg, device_id, identity, checksum).

oneOf.title: capture
oneOf.description: Where a recognised message is read: the value is kept under this name.

recognised_frame_token.description: An element of a message recognised: a byte, the word any (any byte), a capture, or an object of one key of its nature (arg, device_id, identity, checksum).

expr.description: A value computed from the arguments, a byte of MIDI data from 0 to 127 as the engine bounds it: add, sub and mul give their result bounded to 0..127; gt, lt, eq and ne give 0 or 1; if gives its second operand when the first is not 0, else its third.

name.description: The model's name, as its maker writes it.

revision.description: The version this file describes (firmware or document).

manufacturer_id.description: The maker's SysEx id: one byte, or three starting with 0.

rate_limit_hz.description: Most messages a second the device takes; 0: no limit known.

stands_for.description: The catalogue address maker/device of the device a virtual instrument stands for; only a software device gives it.

fidelity.description: How true a virtual instrument is to the device it stands for: faithful (the real firmware, emulated), modelled (the behaviour reproduced from study, without its firmware), principle (a design that follows the device's principle without claiming its behaviour). Needs stands_for.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

transport.description: How a software is reached (OSC host and ports).

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

profile.description: A maker profile this extends (maker or maker/family).

request.description: The identify request, when not the Universal Identity Request (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7); its elements may take the device's own values (an identity object).

to.description: Where the request goes: every_port (default), or named_ports, only the ports whose name matches ports (for a message other devices might misread).

script.description: A Lua script that says whether a reply is this device's, for what reply cannot say: it reads reply (the bytes, from 1) and returns true or false; with reply, both must hold. Requires the lua capability.

reply.description: The start of the reply, element by element: a byte, any, a capture, or an object of its nature.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

decode.description: How the bytes read as a version. A closed list, with no extension: raw_bytes, json (needs field), korg_minor_major, yamaha_tenths, ascii, lua (needs script).

field.description: With decode json: the reply from the offset in at to F7 is a JSON object, and the version is this key's text.

script.description: With decode lua: the script that reads the version from the reply.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

firmware.description: Where the reply carries the firmware version, and how to read it.

ports.description: Its port names, for a device that does not answer.

usb.description: Its USB identities (one per model version or mode): the strongest sign of which model is plugged in, read by a native program (a web browser does not see it).

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

identity.description: How to recognise the device and its firmware: its answer to an identify request, its port names, its USB identity, what it sends by itself. The controls it sends when its knobs are turned are its cc_params and params.

writable.description: Whether the bank can be written; absent, it can. false is a bank a tool reads and never writes.

selects.description: What a bank selects: the sound kind's list, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as a plain recall).

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

osc.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix.

default.description: The raw value of the control on an initialised sound, in the space of range (the 14 bits of a cc + cc_lsb pair; orientation does not recentre it). The reader refuses a default outside range, bounds included; without range it is compared to nothing.

priority.description: How important the control is, from 1 (essential) to 5 (hidden), as priority of MIDI-CI Property Exchange (M2-117-UM).

step_count.description: The number of distinct steps of the control, 2 or more (stepCount of M2-117-UM).

transmit.description: Whether the control is sent as absolute values, relative values, both or none (transmit of M2-117-UM).

recognize.description: Whether the control is recognised as absolute values, relative values, both or none (recognize of M2-117-UM).

values.description: Named values, each label with its integer. The reader refuses a value outside range, bounds included; without range it is compared to nothing.

expects.description: What the control expects: continuous (default), switch, momentary, trigger, clock or discrete, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as continuous).

transform.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua expression applied to the value.

also.description: The ways of reaching the control after the one the flat fields give (cc, cc_lsb, nrpn_msb, nrpn_lsb, rpn_msb, rpn_lsb, range), in the order of preference: a sender picks the first way it can send, a receiver recognises all of them as the same control, a reader never reorders them. A message (kind, channel, numbers) is claimed once, across the ways and across the controls; the reader refuses a second claim at the later place.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

cc_way.description: One way of reaching a control: a CC (with cc_lsb for 14 bits), an NRPN or an RPN, with its own range. One message kind only.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

recognize.description: Whether the control is recognised as absolute values, relative values, both or none (recognize of M2-117-UM).

forward.description: The OSC message sent to a software; {"arg": name} takes an argument of the command, {"capture": name} a capture.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

pre.description: Values computed from the arguments before the message is built (split a number into bytes).

script.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua script that changes the message before it is sent.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

osc.description: The control's address, read the same way from one device to the next (/filter/cutoff), after the device's prefix.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

match_frame.description: A message recognised, element by element: a byte, any, a capture, or an object of its nature.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

emit_osc.description: The address it is reported at: a string without space or brace, or segments whose captures take the message's captured fields.

emit_args.description: The OSC arguments it is reported with, in order; absent: none.

script.description: osc-bridge extension: a Lua script that reads the message.

^_.description: A note for people (provenance, caveats, usage); never read by a program.

type.description: What kind of source: one of the 14 terms of the README, or an extension x-<registrant>-<term> (read as the lowest reliability).

firmware.description: The firmware the source documents; unknown when it does not say.

license.description: An SPDX licence id (by its shape), public-domain, NOASSERTION (SPDX: the source states no licence; nothing is asserted) or NONE (SPDX: the source declares that it grants no licence). SPDX's two special values are written in capitals; other spellings are refused.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.
A note for people; never read by a program.

sends.description: What the device sends by itself, unasked: habits that tell models apart.

active_sensing.description: Sends Active Sensing (FE) about every 300 ms.

clock.description: Sends MIDI clock (F8) even when stopped.
